author: LegalEagle
description:
Don’t expect a season of bipartisan handshakes between Trump and the new Congress 🥊

Back in 2024, Trump warned that if Democrats won, “You might get thrown into a system where everyone has healthcare.” He said it because he opposes universal healthcare, which makes a bipartisan path to Medicare for All hard to imagine.

Three days after the election, Trump named Stephen Miller, the architect of his mass deportation agenda, as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Presumptive incoming Speaker Hakeem Jeffries responded that he has zero interest in working with Miller, and Representative Robert Garcia, the incoming Oversight chair, said in a statement that Miller should lawyer up.

Meanwhile, the president says he has ordered the Justice Department to look into what he calls criminal acts by Democrats. With both sides drawing lines this early, a fight looks far more likely than compromise.

Follow us for more legal breakdowns as this unfolds!

#Congress #StephenMiller #Hake
title: Why Trump and the New Congress Are Likely Headed for a Fight
